statement: For independent Bernoulli(p) bond percolation, n pairwise edge-disjoint finite x-y cutsets F_i imply P_p(x connected to y) <= product_i[1-(1-p)^|F_i|].
proof_or_counterexample: Connection requires an open edge in every F_i; the corresponding sigma-fields are mutually independent.

statement: An infinite connected locally finite vertex-transitive graph with arbitrarily many pairwise edge-disjoint uniformly bounded o-y_n cuts satisfies p_u=1.
assumptions: n such cuts separate o,y_n for every n
proof_or_counterexample: Unique infinite-cluster membership gives tau_p(o,y_n)>=theta_p^2 by Harris; L1 gives decay to zero for p<1.
remaining_gap: The cut hypothesis is not supplied by general nonamenability; independent review pending.

statement: For a connected locally finite one-ended graph with maximum degree d and edge Cheeger constant h_E>0, the number of disjoint x-y cuts of size at most K is at most d(|B_R(x)|+|B_R(y)|), R=ceil(K/h_E)+1. This is uniform in x,y on vertex-transitive graphs.
proof_or_counterexample: Reduce cuts to minimal cuts; each has a finite endpoint component of volume <=K/h_E. All cuts use edges near x or y, a uniformly finite supply in a transitive graph.
remaining_gap: Parent conjecture requires a different merger-control mechanism on one-ended Cayley graphs; independent review pending.

statement: For m>=3 and the simple Cayley graph of C_2*C_m with S={a,b,b^-1}, h_E>=1-2/m>0, p_u=1, and p_c is the unique p in (0,1) solving p[2 sum_{k=1}^{m-1}p^k-(m-1)p^m]=1.
assumptions: One undirected a-edge per involution pair
proof_or_counterexample: Free-product normal form gives a tree of disjoint cycle blocks. Fresh block-cluster exploration has offspring Bin(X-1,p), with exact mean. Bridge cutsets give two-point decay; L2 proves pu=1. Cyclomatic counting gives the Cheeger bound.
remaining_gap: No general generating-set or one-ended extension; no novelty claim; review pending.

statement: For an infinite connected d-regular vertex-transitive undirected graph and normalized walk operator P=A/d with rho=||P||_2, pd rho<1 implies tau_p(x,y)<=(pd rho)^dist(x,y)/(1-pd rho), so pu>=1/(d rho). Thus pc<1/(d rho) suffices for pc<pu, without being necessary.
assumptions: Vertex transitivity for the uniqueness conclusion
proof_or_counterexample: Use union bound on simple open paths, then upper-bound their count by A^n matrix entries <=d^n rho^n; Harris contradicts uniqueness when the bound decays. Repeated-edge walks are not assigned probability p^n.
remaining_gap: No universal proof that pc<1/(d rho); this criterion even fails to certify T3's genuine nonuniqueness interval.

statement: The normalized-rho reduction pc<1/rho in C0047-A001 is vacuous when rho<1, because pc<=1<1/rho; its proposed remaining case pc>=1/rho is impossible. The degree factor is required in L5's elementary sufficient criterion.
assumptions: rho is the normalized simple-random-walk spectral radius, as explicitly specified in A001
proof_or_counterexample: pc is in [0,1], whereas 1/rho>1. On T3, rho=2sqrt(2)/3, pc=1/2 and pu=1; the valid sufficient threshold 1/(3rho) is below pc.
remaining_gap: Source correction not yet applied; does not refute or solve C0047.
